 Most recent Most popular Good night published at 20:21 GMT 31 October 20:21 GMT 31 October 
 We'll leave it here.
 Rangers have booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup final after an 83rd-minute goal from Ryan Naderi broke Aberdeen's brave resistance at Hampden.
 Thanks for your company and enjoy your Saturday night.
 Image source, SNS 
 44 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Stage set for Edinburgh duo published at 20:16 GMT 31 October 20:16 GMT 31 October 
 Who will Rangers face in the final on 13 December? 
 Hearts and Hibs go at it at Hampden tomorrow.
 The Jambos have won all four Edinburgh derbies at the national stadium and are currently in a much better place than their rivals, with Hibs at the bottom of the Premiership and still seeking a first win under Marink Reedijk.
 What a time it would be for the Dutchman to break that duck.
 That one is a 15:00 GMT kick-off.
 15 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Robinson 'very proud' of Aberdeen effort published at 20:14 GMT 31 October 20:14 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson tells BBC Scotland: "I think we did more than hang in there. 
 "It's easy to make excuses with the amount of injuries we had defensively and I thought Jack Milne was outstanding. He comes in for a lot of criticism but I thought he was outstanding today, as was Nicky Devlin. 
 "We said that's the level of performance, the energy and work ethic to push us forward. It can't just be for a semi-final.
 "Unfortunately, we've picked up another two defensive injuries. It's a blow, we've not had our troubles to seek in that area.
 "The players were very well organised, they bought into it. We had one day to work on it. I'm very proud of them, they're a great group of boys. I love working with them. That effort and work rate is the bare minimum.
 "We probably won't get positives, we lost the game so that will be the narrative. We have to win on Saturday [home to Hibernian] to give us some breathing space before the international break where we can try and get bodies back."
 Image source, SNS 
 20 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Rangers show resilience again - Penrice published at 20:07 GMT 31 October 20:07 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Rangers' James Penrice tells Premier Sports: "I thought we stuck in there and got our goal, a proper striker's goal from Ryan [Naderi].
 "You've seen this season the resilience to keep going. We're buzzing to get into the final and that's the main thing. 
 "We've turned a corner but it's still not completely there."
 Image source, SNS

 'I need to work on shooting' published at 20:02 GMT 31 October 20:02 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Player-of-the-match Badredine Bouanani tells Premier Sports: "Everyone played well and I'm so happy to win. 
 "I had a few chances, I need to work on shooting. I think I should have scored one or two goals today but I will work on that in training. 
 "I'm very happy to get the win. Let's move forward."

 The Czech Republic international, signed from the German third tier, is developing a good habit of being in the right place at the right time.

 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen

 That one was 1-0 too.
 132 45 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Important opportunity for us' - McInnes published at 19:53 GMT 31 October 19:53 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Rangers manager Derek McInnes tells Premier Sports: "Semi-finals are never easy. 
 "Our play was too ponderous in the first half, we needed to move quicker across the grass. It's embarrassing we had 25 shots and only five on target. Thankfully Ryan [Naderi] scores a scruffy goal, he anticipates a shot going across the goal and thankfully he managed to get the goal that matters for us. 
 "I thought we were far more imposing in the second half than in the first. I always felt like a goal was coming but I was more concerned about giving one away at the other end. 
 "I always feel there's a goal in us but we can't be as vulnerable as we were in transition. 
 "We've invested a lot in the forward line but there's times where we maybe need an older head. We were too snatchy at crosses and I don't think we take full advantage of some of our attacking play. 
 "Thankfully one [goal] was enough for us today. It's an important opportunity for us now to go and build a bit of confidence by winning a trophy."

 'Aberdeen strikers let side down' published at 19:48 GMT 31 October 19:48 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Willie Miller 
Former Aberdeen captain on BBC Sportsound 
 I thought Stephen Robinson got his tactics right and made it extremely difficult for Rangers. I don't think Rangers showed their quality for the vast majority of the game and that made it scrappy.
 The Aberdeen strikers were so poor. The game was made easy for the Rangers defenders because of the lack of quality from Nisbet and Mouloua. You need your strikers to be able to hold it up and give it a little bit of respite. 
 It was probably a Stephen Robinson type of game, he was hoping to frustrate the opposition and get an opportunity. 
 Overall, I think Aberdeen put up a fine show and he can be pleased with his players.

 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Tom English 
BBC Scotland's chief sports writer 
 Rangers deservedly won the game.They slowly turned the screw and you could sense that there was a goal coming. They made hard work of it but they stuck to their task and they're in the final. 
 I think we saw why Aberdeen have gone six out of 11 games in the league without scoring. That's a big problem for them.

 'Just trying to enjoy it' - Raskin published at 19:39 GMT 31 October 19:39 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Rangers midfielder Nicolas Raskin tells Premier Sports: "It feels good. 
 "I think the team showed a lot of character in the second half. They had a brilliant goalkeeper who made a lot of saves. 
 "I'm so happy for Ryan [Naderi] to get the goal. 
 "It's about trying to be a bit more clinical and putting the ball into the net.
 "I know we dropped a couple of points recently but we're still 11 games unbeaten, still enjoying the moment. There's always tough times in a season, we're just trying to enjoy it. 
 "We want to come back here and win the cup."

 'It was just a matter of time before we scored' published at 19:33 GMT 31 October 19:33 GMT 31 October 
 FT: Rangers 1-0 Aberdeen 
 Rangers goalscorer Ryan Naderi tells Premier Sports: "[It's] wonderful. I'm so happy.
 "I'm happy for the team, we deserved it. It was just a question of when we would score, we did and I'm so happy we did, we deserved it. 
 "I always try to stay onside, sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't, I'm glad it worked this time. 
 "I felt it was just a matter of time before we scored. We had so much pressure, so many shots on target and I just felt like we would score. 
 "I enjoy playing up front with Kevin Kelsy but also the whole team, it's fun to be on the pitch with those guys."

 At a glance 
 Late Naderi goal proves difference at Hampden
 McInnes' side extend unbeaten run to 11 games
 Rangers will play Hearts or Hibs in final on 13 December
 By Martin Dowden BBC Sport Scotland at Hampden Rangers reached the League Cup final after Ryan Naderi's late strike at Hampden finally breached a stubborn Aberdeen. 
 The win extends the Ibrox side's unbeaten run to 11 games, with either Hibernian or Hearts the obstacle in the final on 13 December as they seek their first silverware under boss Derek McInnes.
 For all the positives among Aberdeen's performance, it is a fourth loss in five and a missed opportunity for manager Stephen Robinson to secure a much-needed statement win and enhance his own fine cup record.
 Aberdeen last lifted this trophy under McInnes in 2014. Their wait goes on with Rangers within touching distance of capitalising on their impressive recent run of results.
 The odds were stacked against the Pittodrie side with many believing this to be a formality, a routine stroll for Rangers. Not so.
 Defensively depleted, Aberdeen still looked strong - albeit Ayoub Mouloua was a touch fortunate to escape an early handball.
 Rangers had no shots on target until the 43rd minute but then went close three times before the break and swarmed all over their opponents after it, with Badredine Bouanani a constant threat.
 Aberdeen held firm impressively until the breakthrough arrived late on with Naderi touching home after good work from Kevin Kelsy and James Penrice.
 Rangers analysis: Bouanani & Naderi make mark 
 Heavy favourites coming into this, Rangers had the opportunity to reach a final and cement recent progress with a shot at silverware.
 Despite their long unbeaten run, and Aberdeen's troubles, they struggled to impose themselves where it counted - converting chances. The performance was lacking first half and chances not executed when they came.
 That said, they moved through the gears and exerted sustained pressure after the break, with Bouanani a standout, offering genuine and consistent threat.
 Naderi, once again, made a telling contribution in a season where he has stood up after initial doubts over his ability to be a regular starter.
 McInnes stated this was no formality and it proved the case. Semi-finals often play-out this way with the stakes so high. Job done in the end and it was deserved.
 For Rangers, and McInnes, it is another big outcome that adds even more promise to a season that looks very much on the right track.
 Aberdeen analysis: Game plan effective but Dons come up short 
 Robinson said pre-match that Aberdeen had nothing to lose given the expectations. Trying to seize something positive from being strong underdogs. The first half was very positive.
 The game plan worked and they looked fairly solid at the back. When blocks were required, blocks were produced. That continued after the break when they were under siege at times.
 What they lacked was a focal point up front. That ultimately let them down.
 Robinson pointed to his managerial cup record, and rightly so, having won this trophy last term with St Mirren. He got a response but it just was not enough to secure what would have been such an important win for him and the club.
 Whether that appeases increasing doubters within the Aberdeen fanbase remains to be seen but they can take a degree of positivity for how they performed.
 What they said 
 Figure caption, 'Better team won' - McInnes on semi-final victory
 Rangers manager Derek McInnes: "Our play was too ponderous in the first half, we needed to move quicker across the grass. It's embarrassing that we had 25 shots and only five on target. 
 "Thankfully Ryan [Naderi] scores a scruffy goal, he anticipates a shot going across the goal and thankfully he managed to get the goal that matters for us.
 "I thought we were far more imposing in the second half than in the first. I always felt like a goal was coming but I was more concerned about giving one away at the other end.
 "Thankfully one [goal] was enough for us today. It's an important opportunity for us now to go and build a bit of confidence by winning a trophy."
 Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson: "I think we did more than hang in there. We said that's the level of performance, the energy and work ethic to push us forward. It can't just be for a semi-final.
 "Unfortunately we've picked up another two defensive injuries. It's a blow, we've not had our troubles to seek in that area.
 "We probably won't get positives, we lost the game so that will be the narrative. We have to win on Saturday [home to Hibernian] to give us some breathing space before the international break where we can try and get bodies back."
